title: Plan throttles, emergency fallback & credit-visibility PRD
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Define and roll out a plan-level soft-throttle + emergency fallback mechanism with transparent credit visibility in the Console and invoice-safe billing acceptance criteria. This PRD captures requirements for product, edge-case billing rules, UX for credits and remaining allowances, SLO implications, and the operational runbook for incidents. Goals: 1) Prevent noisy tenant spikes from taking down shared hosted clusters by introducing per-plan soft throttles that reduce throughput gracefully while preserving a best-effort baseline; 2) Provide clear credit visibility (real-time remaining credits, projected exhaustion time, billing preview) in the Console and via API; 3) Implement an emergency fallback model routing policy to move traffic to compatible lower-cost/latency tiers without incurring unexpected charges; 4) Define acceptance criteria that guarantee invoice clarity and automatic reconciliation behavior for transient throttles and fallback-induced overage. Non-goals: changes to core token pricing, permanent entitlement migration automation, and new payment flows.
scope: MVP covers hosted API customers on pay-as-you-go and committed tiers. Include per-route and per-caller rate-limit caps mapped to plan entitlements and a soft-throttle window (configurable: 30s-5m). Console UI surfaces: remaining credits, per-route throttle status, projected exhaust time, and billing preview. API surface: endpoints for credit balance, throttle state, and opt-in emergency fallback ruleset. Ops: realtime alerting and a manual override in Console. Billing: define how short-duration fallbacks are shown on invoices and an automated shortfall credit policy for incidents under 24h.
out_of_scope: Dedicated & Private control plane changes (will be tracked separately), new KMS integrations, per-token price changes, and changes to current entitlements data model schema beyond read-only exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-throttle enforcement: For customers exceeding plan throughput, system returns a 429-like soft-throttle signal with Retry-After semantics and a streamed header informing of remaining credits; throttles must not drop existing open streams unless explicitly requested by the customer.

Emergency fallback: When capacity constraints occur, traffic can be routed to a lower-priority model tier that preserves function but may increase latency; fallback must be logged and shown in Console with start/end timestamps and cost delta estimate.
Credit visibility: Console and billing-preview API show current credit balance, 7-day burn rate projection, and predicted exhaustion date; the data must update within 30s of usage events.

Invoice clarity: Any cost increases due to fallback or transient overage are grouped under a discrete invoice line item with clear tags ("fallback-usage" or "soft-overage") and a reconciliation link; customers receive an automated email for billing-impacting fallback events exceeding $50.

Shortfall auto-credit: For platform incidents that cause forced throttles or routed fallbacks lasting under 24h, ops can trigger an automated shortfall credit that applies to the next invoice; the acceptance test must simulate an incident and validate credit application and delta reporting.
API parity: Programmatic endpoints return the same throttle state and credit numbers shown in Console within 60s under normal load.

Telemetry: Rate-limits, throttle triggers, fallback events, and credit adjustments are emitted to the observability pipeline with tags for customer_id, plan_id, route, and region; all events retained for 90 days.

Rollout: Feature flag gating exists per-tenant and per-route; rollout in three waves (internal beta, 5% customers, 100%) with canary monitoring that aborts if error-rate increases by >2x or latency P95 worsens by >200ms for two consecutive windows.
Docs & UX: Console help text, billing FAQ, and API docs published before 5% rollout. UX copy for throttled response and fallback must be approved by Design.
Security: No new customer secrets are introduced; access to credit APIs respect existing RBAC and SSO rules.
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Decided on soft-throttle vs hard-block to minimize user surprise; soft-throttle chosen to preserve UX and enable graceful degradation.
2026-02-18: Chose to implement emergency fallback as routing to a pre-defined lower-priority model variant rather than on-the-fly quantization to reduce runtime risk.
2026-02-22: Agreed throttles will surface a 'projected exhaust' metric in Console and via API; engineering committed to 30s propagation SLA for credit updates.
2026-02-25: Billing team required that fallback-induced costs be labeled separately on invoices — added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-28: Opted to limit automated shortfall credits to incidents <24h and to require Ops runbook entry for manual credits beyond that window.
implementation_notes: Backend: extend entitlement service to expose remaining credit streaming endpoint; add throttle controller in gateway to emit soft-throttle headers and diagnostics.
Routing: update smart router policies to include fallback candidates and cost-estimation hook; fallback must be reversible within 60s.
Billing: tagging layer to mark fallback/soft-overage usage; invoice microservice to aggregate and show labeled line items.
Console: new CreditStatus panel and per-route throttle indicator; add manual override toggle for Ops with audit logging.
Telemetry: ensure new events integrate with existing alerting dashboards and SLOs; create fallback-specific dashboards and a billing anomalies dashboard.
Testing: end-to-end scenarios including long-tail burst, cross-region failover, and synthetic high-burst tests; include load tests that validate 429s are rate-limited but streams remain intact.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may be confused by fallback costs. Mitigation: clear Console messaging, pre-rollout emails, and separate invoice lines with reconciliation links.
Risk: Telemetry lag could cause mismatched credit displays. Mitigation: initial SLA of 30s propagation and fallback to conservative estimate if telemetry delayed.
Risk: Fallback may increase latency or change output quality. Mitigation: limit to compatible model variants with documented performance profiles and include customer opt-out.
Risk: Incorrect shortfall credit application. Mitigation: require Ops approval flow for credits >$500 and automated test coverage for reconciliation path.
rollout_plan: Internal beta (week 1): test with 3 internal high-throughput tenants, validate metrics and reconciliation flow.
Canary 5% (week 2-3): enable for small subset of customers by plan type; monitor billing deltas and UX signals; require manual 'go/no-go'.
Gradual 100% (week 4): expand after 3 successful canary windows; enable self-serve opt-in for early adopters in Console.
Post-launch: 30-day review to evaluate billing disputes, usage patterns, and potential adjustments to soft-throttle thresholds.
